title: Johnson, Gray, Goldsmith - poets of the mid-eighteenth century

vibeProfile.oneLine: A critical guide to the mid-eighteenth-century poetry of Johnson, Gray and Goldsmith.

summary: A critical study of three major poets of the mid-eighteenth century: Samuel Johnson, Thomas Gray and Oliver Goldsmith, whose meditative and moral verse bridges the Augustan age and the coming Romantic era. Prepared as a student's companion, it offers context and close readings of poems like Gray's famous 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'. A helpful scholarly guide to a quieter, reflective period of English poetry often overshadowed by what came before and after.
whyReadIt: A scholarly guide to Johnson, Gray and Goldsmith, the reflective poets bridging the Augustan and Romantic ages.

funFacts.text: Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' is among the most quoted poems in English.
